6. @JacquelynGill shares another good news story to pull you out of the Franzen-pit of despair. Handing over power to women may be just the antidote we need, both for his brand of all-encompassing/enervating misery, and finding our way thru #climatecrisis https://t.co/QmvrNuDptt

Science/activism ethical balance question: If one is unable to join the #ClimateStrike today because one is committed to a research meeting where #climatechange will definitely be on the agenda, is going to work for that still considered crossing the picket line? https://t.co/jjSopvSGlR
Finally!! The @GretaThunberg Helpline… because when it comes to #climatechange we all know she’s the real problem! https://t.co/rggkV3POhi via @abc730 @Fridays4future
‘Know My Name,’ a Sexual Assault Survivor Tells the World https://t.co/fdn4V6Ucz9 - @jenniferweiner reviews Chanel Miller’s powerful book. #MeToo
Yes. Quite. Cricket needs to take #climatechange seriously - Ian Chappell via ⁦@ESPNcricinfo⁩ https://t.co/9yHzRmjAK2

It is moving to see fellow scientists in the academic diaspora rightfully mourn the loss of beloved places to #climatechange. Yet… how long have indigenous + marginalized people been witnessing even deeper losses due to the dominant “civilization” of which our science is a part?

But… talk about the #climatechange pigeons coming home to roost, for the legacy of the guy who removed solar panels from the roof of the White House! If only the fire could cleanse the last 4 decades of history and give us a reboot into a different timeline… sigh…

Temperature and humidity and vegetation growth are only part of the story. We have to address the history of colonial expansion and science, along with the technologies and economic models that are directly implicated in climate change. #ClimateChange #CaliforniaFires
The day it forgot to rain on Australia https://t.co/ta7GjahPkc via @smh #ClimateChange #ClimateCrisis

#science4climate David O’Malley (USGS) brings his wisdom from a career in #climatechange research. “30 yrs ago, we thought climate adaptation meant surrender! I no longer think that.” The #sagegrouse on his cover slide reminds me of @canislatrans tweet: https://t.co/b2qk6ceUGs https://t.co/NrzECQxKoI

#science4climate Dr. Thornbrugh: We are seeing ecosystems and many of things we are connected with moving with #climatechange but our ability to move with them is constrained as tribal nations have been forced to become fixed; a territorial expansion framework is very important https://t.co/S6KttJAsv4

Surreal to see this as we sit in New Orleans in a @se_casc #science4climate symposium session on going from studying #climatechange impacts to adaptation. 
'Venice Is On Its Knees': Mayor Blames Worst Flood Tide In 50 Years On Climate Change https://t.co/brrIsCZnjU

Rosina Philippe (Atakapa- Ishak/Chawasha, Grand Bayou) draws upon creation stories to remind us that we are the youngest species and therefore must remember our place in life’s full circle. On issues of land loss and #climatechange: “we are engaged!” #science4climate https://t.co/xTXgqoAx5H

Funny thing about accelerating #climatechange: the clapbacks from nature also come fast and hard.
Italian council is flooded immediately after rejecting measures on climate change - CNN https://t.co/Easxd5gwmD

Gosh, and what an emergency is this one where even the dictionary accepts two words as one! Appropriate also, I suppose, for the age when the two word phrase is literally mushed together on here more often than not: #ClimateEmergency

Damn right. The global industrial capitalist system loves nothing more than putting the burden of solving the collective problems created by big corporations on individuals whom they have left with very limited power. #climatecrisis

But we cannot get out of this hole of environmental degradation if we don’t assert collective power through our democratic institutions to regulate industry and reign in corporations and oligarchs who only care about short-term profits. #climatecrisis

@kavita_krishnan @AparajitaDatta4 Yes he is owed compensation. But the recent history of #BlackLivesMatter activism suggests you are too optimistic about what may happen in the US, alas.

Legislative action + regulations are essential to address #ClimateChange. Individual steps to reduce our footprints won’t take us anywhere near far enough towards reducing emissions when this capitalist economy is still hurtling in the opposite direction.
 https://t.co/fLI4loZoz8
